title: Functional hard-sphere fluctuations on a regular Boltzmann lifespan
abstract_tex:
We prove a path-space upgrade of the finite-dimensional hard-sphere
fluctuation theorem on an entire supplied regular Boltzmann interval.
The setting is the deterministic, nonequilibrium, grand-canonical gas in
three-dimensional whole space, with exact microscopic centering and no time
smoothing. Relative to the pinned finite-history interfaces, one collective
time translation of a connected history gives a shrinking-window factor at
its sharp factorial-cumulant scale. This also localizes redundant contacts,
whose times are determined rather than independent coordinates. A
prefix-measurable global chronology indicator is retained through the
translation and the flux-tree estimate. Initial-link cylinders preserve the
connected activity scale, and a fixed Gaussian reserve keeps summability
independent of the later moment order. A decorated final-slab output kernel
controls the number of jumping particles. Third moments at scale
$\mu^{-3/2}$, dyadic chaining, and a uniform exact-centering comparison yield
$J_1$ convergence and C-tightness for every finite vector of compact smooth
tests, with the Gaussian covariance of the credited finite-dimensional theorem.
abstract_plain_text: We prove a path-space upgrade of the finite-dimensional hard-sphere fluctuation theorem on an entire supplied regular Boltzmann interval. The setting is the deterministic, nonequilibrium, grand-canonical gas in three-dimensional whole space, with exact microscopic centering and no time smoothing. Relative to the pinned finite-history interfaces, one collective time translation of a connected history gives a shrinking-window factor at its sharp factorial-cumulant scale. This also localizes redundant contacts, whose times are determined rather than independent coordinates. A prefix-measurable global chronology indicator is retained through the translation and the flux-tree estimate. Initial-link cylinders preserve the connected activity scale, and a fixed Gaussian reserve keeps summability independent of the later moment order. A decorated final-slab output kernel controls the number of jumping particles. Third moments at scale mu^(-3/2), dyadic chaining, and a uniform exact-centering comparison yield J1 convergence and C-tightness for every finite vector of compact smooth tests, with the Gaussian covariance of the credited finite-dimensional theorem.
comments: This is an AI-assisted preprint with internal independent agent proof, contribution and manuscript reviews, not external peer review. Supporting Lean material is partial and does not formalize the complete theorem. Mathematical results from OpenAI/math at revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb are stipulated premises, with exact source interfaces and other credited inputs disclosed in the paper. The literature comparison is bounded and does not certify worldwide priority. Nine supporting Lean declarations concern collision energy, affine shifts and exponent arithmetic; fourteen independent audit declarations and four rejected mutations support that narrow audit. History existence, chronology, Jacobians, analytic estimates, tightness and the full path theorem are not formalized. Public DOI/package URL to be added only after actual publication.
